exercises.question: According to the essay *La unidad dentro de la diversidad*, why does no single country hold a monopoly on 'correct' pronunciation?
options: Because the educated norm of Spanish is pluricentric, so features like Latin American seseo and the peninsular distinction enjoy equal prestige.
Because the national academies decided to eliminate all pronunciation rules and allow speakers to spell words according to their local accent.
Because spoken Spanish has already split into mutually unintelligible regional languages that share only a historical name and origin.
Because only international broadcasters who avoid both seseo and voseo are recognized as models of the educated spoken standard today.

exercises.question: What contrast does paragraph 3 of the essay draw regarding object pronouns across the Hispanic world?
options: Latin America preserves the lo/la vs. le distinction, while parts of Spain use leísmo—accepted only for a singular male person, whereas laísmo and loísmo are rejected.
Latin America uses laísmo and loísmo in formal writing, while central and northern Spain strictly preserve lo, la, and le according to syntactic function in every context.
The academies recently accepted both laísmo and loísmo in formal academic prose while rejecting singular male-person leísmo across the entire Spanish-speaking world.
Object pronouns are the one area of Spanish grammar where no historical or regional differences exist between peninsular varieties and Latin American varieties.

exercises.question: According to the essay, what allows some twenty Spanish-speaking nations to keep up fluent communication despite their regional variants?
options: A shared spelling system, a common formal register, and the cooperative work of the academies in recording regional variants in a shared dictionary.
A mandatory editorial policy requiring all international universities and newspapers to replace Latin American vocabulary with peninsular words.
The gradual disappearance of voseo, tuteo, and ustedeo from everyday family conversation across both Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula.
The requirement that every scientist, judge, and journalist write exclusively in colloquial local idioms when publishing for an international audience.

prompt.speaker: Meg
prompt.text: Después de leer el ensayo, me queda claro que ningún acento nacional es superior a otro, pero ¿qué ocurre cuando redactamos un texto académico internacional?

options: En ese caso se adopta un registro formal compartido, de modo que cualquier lector hispanohablante comprenda el texto con total claridad.
En ese caso todo aquel que redacte un texto académico debes usar un registro formal compartido para que cualquier lector lo comprenda.
En ese caso se exige usar el laísmo y el loísmo en cada párrafo para demostrar un uso culto del idioma.
En ese caso quienes escribe un ensayo formal deben evitar los giros locales para que cualquier lector lo comprenda.
